review.notes: Text lineage v0 (FET-EN017, 2005-03-01) -> v1 (DR3-EN137, 2006-11-25) -> v2 (AP01-EN014, 2012-11-23) is cosmetic: "sent to the Graveyard as a result of battle" -> "destroyed by battle and sent to the Graveyard", "any \"Hyena\"(s)" -> "any number of \"Hyenas\"", and the dropped "Then shuffle your Deck." procedural line. Both scripts use the identical EVENT_BATTLE_DESTROYED condition and the same multi-summon operation including the CARD_BLUEEYES_SPIRIT clamp. Packet/repo note: the packet's script_diff renders the goat name filter as `c:IsCode(MODID)` while the shipped goat/c504700034.lua uses the literal `c:IsCode(22873798)`; both are equivalent to modern's `c:IsCode(id)` because the goat file's own `id` is 504700034 - a rendering artifact, not a behavioural difference. Verification-half bounds: old attested through 2011-02-02, modern from 2019-04-03.

event.historical_text: When this card is sent to the Graveyard as a result of battle, you can Special Summon any "Hyena"(s) from the Deck to the field. Then shuffle your Deck.
event.summary: Period ruling package, not a text erratum. Activation condition: the modern `s.target` requires another "Hyena" to exist in the Deck (`Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard(s.filter,tp,LOCATION_DECK,...)`), while the goat target only checks `Duel.GetLocationCount(tp,LOCATION_MZONE)>0`, so the battle-destruction trigger may be used with no copy left. Failed-search verification: the goat operation adds `else Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)` to prove the whiff by revealing the Deck. Only the verification half is covered by the shared search-verification chronology, so the combined transition is recorded unresolved.
